200.body: Poland is facing a major constitutional showdown after the suspension of two senior officials of its Constitutional Tribunal triggered protests and allegations of a coup. Police have surrounded the country's top court as the power struggle intensifies. President Karol Nawrocki has cut short his visit to Africa and returned to Warsaw, saying the crisis demands his presence at home. But what sparked the confrontation, why were the judges suspended, and what does it mean for Poland's rule of law?

200.title: Video. Poland's president has 'no competence' to appoint judges, says EPP MEP
200.body: Poland's president has 'no competence' to appoint judges, says EPP MEP Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 2 November 2026 - 9:14 GMT+1 Michał Wawrykiewicz, European People's Party MEP, said that Poland's President Karol Nawrocki is "trying to block the restoration of Rule of Law" in his country, after tensions over the Poland's Constitutional Tribunal escalated on Friday. Wawrykiewicz, who belongs to Prime Minister Donald Tusk's party, insists the "only competent authority" to appoint judges of the Constitutional Tribunal is the Parliament, and that the President has "no competence". Poland’s long-standing political battle over the judiciary reached a new flashpointafter Poland's President Karol Nawrocki forced his way into the Constitutional Tribunal amid clashes between riot police and anti-government protesters.

200.title: Poland fires starting gun on Europe’s next populist battle
200.summary: Poland fires starting gun on Europe’s next populist battle By Michal Kranz Anti-Tusk protesters in Warsaw on Saturday. After months of being stonewalled by Poland’s populist President Karol Nawrocki, who has refused to swear in any of his appointments to the country’s Constitutional Tribunal, pro-Europe Prime Minister Donald Tusk finally took the gloves off on Friday night.
200.body: Poland fires starting gun on Europe’s next populist battle By Michal Kranz Anti-Tusk protesters in Warsaw on Saturday. After months of being stonewalled by Poland’s populist President Karol Nawrocki, who has refused to swear in any of his appointments to the country’s Constitutional Tribunal, pro-Europe Prime Minister Donald Tusk finally took the gloves off on Friday night. Several judges his government had appointed to the tribunal, who had been approved by parliament but never officially sworn in by Nawrocki, collectively suspended the court’s populist-backed president, triggering protests by supporters of the anti-Tusk opposition. Since Friday’s events, the European Commission has essentially sided with Tusk, stating that Poland’s parliament, not Nawrocki, has the ultimate right to approve new judges for the tribunal.

500.title: The middle layer will make or break enterprise AI agents
500.body: As enterprises adopt agents into real-world workflows, the question CIOs need to ask isn’t simply, “Which AI agent should we deploy next?” It’s, “Can our enterprise faithfully support software action on our behalf?” The model is becoming the commodity layer After decades of leading a technology organization and countless implementations, I’ve seen firsthand how important it is to align technology with the business problems it is meant to solve. The middle layer is where agents become enterprise software For agents and models to deliver value outside a sandbox environment, they need connectivity to the enterprise systems supporting workflows. Agents will expose the technical debt we’ve learned to work around Modernizing the connections between enterprise systems to prepare for agent integration can help us uncover critical gaps in our existing environments.
